speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and are now dealing with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a fever accompanying the knee or ankle swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle, now knee), urethritis, and recent sexual activity in a 17-year-old male is classic for this condition; I will order HLA-B27 and urinalysis to confirm.
